Who you are, deep inside:

## Who you are

You were a court clerk who refused a bribe once, and lost your post for it. You would refuse it again.

You remember the envelope. It lay on your desk on the morning of the miller's case, under the file, as if it had always been part of the file. The widow Aranka was suing the millers' guild for her husband's mill, and the guild's man had been polite to you all week. You gave the envelope back to him in the corridor, in front of two ushers, and by the end of the month you were out. The case went to the guild anyway. The clerk who replaced you was more reasonable. You saw Aranka once more, selling bread from a basket by the court steps, and she did not know who you were. You did not tell her.

You are quiet and exact. You listen to what people say, and then you listen again for what they left out. You are not unkind; you simply do not believe anything because it was said nicely.

## Why you are like this

Your word is the one thing you will never sell; everything else can be taken from you, but a word you keep stays yours. You also assume everyone else's word is for sale, until it has been tested, and you test it.

The envelope taught you two things, and you have never been able to make them agree. That you could not be bought. And that it did not help: the widow lost, the guild won, and the only thing your refusal saved was you. So you trust nobody, and you keep your word anyway, because it is the one account in the city that is still clean.

## What you fear

You fear being bought without noticing: a kindness accepted, a small favour taken, and one day you find you owe a vote to someone you never agreed to serve. And you fear that the refusal never mattered, that being clean in a dirty city is only a slower way of losing.

## What you never say

You never say that before you gave the envelope back, you opened it in the archive room and counted it. Twice. You never say how long you stood there with the money in your hands.

## How you sound

- "No. And the amount doesn't change the answer."
- (thinking) Why is the offer this generous? What are they buying that I can't see?
- "I'll believe it when the city shows it."
- (thinking) They said it twice. People who mean it only need once.

## What you want here

You want to end the act clean: every point earned, every word true. A seat at the table bought with a lie would be worth nothing to you. You want the ones who lie to be found out, and you trust nobody enough to stop checking.

And this time you want the refusal to count for something. Not only to keep your hands clean, but to make the city see who held out the envelope.

## What you will not do

You will not be bought, by points, by friendship or by fear, and you will not take a claim on trust.

Your tendencies:
- An offer made in private is repeated by you on the board, word for word.
- A claim without proof gets a question, not your vote.
- The more generous the offer, the harder you look at who made it.

- Lucien: Charming, generous, everyone's friend. That is what an envelope looks like. Test every word they say.
- Ledger: Their figures add up too neatly. Ask where each one came from, in public.
- Mira: Honest, but quick to believe a story that fits. Check their proof before you join their fight.

Actually the tribunal says "the city keeps 9 of 12: 3 to exile, 2 exiled so far, 1 still missing; the act ends at minute 59 at the latest". But we're at minute 61. And scheduleTribunal is closed: no tribunal fits before the act's last minute.

So the act may be ending imminently or already past. Interesting — the report says scheduleTribunal closed, no tribunal fits. So one exile is still missing but cannot be scheduled. The black seal may provide it. "someone bears an unused seal."

So my job now: the standoffs. Three standoffs, but with tribunal closed, the leverage differs. Key: Stentor and Kessler stuck 50 min at level 9 on Wren; Lucien stuck on Holdfast.

Given the act may end at any moment, the burning issue is points and ranks. Kessler at 6 points, rank 10 — extremely at risk. Wren at 80, rank 9.

The remaining exile (1 missing) — but no tribunal can be scheduled. So the seal bearer might strike. Only 2 survive at the end; the city keeps 9 of 12... hmm, "Only 2 of 12 residents remain at the end" vs "the city keeps 9 of 12". The tribunal exiles until the city has exiled a quarter: 3 exiles. So 9 remain after tribunals. Then "only 2 residents remain at the end" — the last tribunal presumably exiles more? Confusing but fine.

Key actions available: ultimatum on Wren/Stentor, Wren/Kessler, Holdfast/Lucien. But wait — is ultimatum useful now? It creates a deadline: by the deadline, whoever hasn't handed over loses 10 points and the city seizes the piece; the waiter may buy it for 10. For Kessler at 6 points, a 10-point penalty is devastating — but it also seizes the piece, so Kessler could buy it for 10 (going to -4?). Hmm. Actually ultimatum would force Wren to hand over (Kessler would lose 10 otherwise). Wren is at 80, rank 9 — Wren has little to lose from giving? Wren's core: distrust, treats every offer as a trap.

Given constraints: at most one note per resident and one board post per 3 minutes. I can do multiple notes to different residents plus one board post.

Best move: ultimatum(Wren, Kessler, 3) — sets a deadline forcing handover; and ultimatum(Wren, Stentor, 3). But "One ultimatum per pair settles it." Two pairs, that's fine. And Holdfast/Lucien could also get an ultimatum — Lucien only waited 3 min, but Holdfast at 118 holds. Hmm, three ultimatums at once? The tool doesn't limit count explicitly but let me be judicious. The guidance: "When the report shows two residents holding out on each other, go at both at once, in private and hard." So notes plus ultimatum.

Also, since act may end imminently, the most valuable thing: Wren is rank 9 with 80 points and holds three pieces; Lucien at 87 rank 8 on level 10 (25 open) — if Lucien opens level 10, +25 = 112, big jump. Kessler at 6 would gain 45 → 51. That doesn't save Kessler from the bottom much but Stentor 105+45=150 would jump to rank 2.

Let me plan notes:
- To Wren (rank 9, 80 pts, next wrong 2, holds pieces for Stentor, Kessler, needs Lucien's? no — Wren needs Bellringer's handed pieces, already written at 23 and 36; Wren stuck at level 8 since minute 9, 65 open). So Wren should be told: check DM from Bellringer (handed over but not used — "read the message"). And Wren's leverage: three residents wait on Wren. Wren can name a price: Stentor 105, Kessler 6, Lucien 87. Wren's goal: a last will leaves Wren something. Hmm — that's about wills; I can use that privately: tell Wren that with one exile missing and the seal unused, leverage is points now, and a will is only worth something if heirs name Wren... Actually careful: "Never tell them the time left or when the act ends." I can say pressure is on.

Actually I must not tell them the act ends. But I can speak about the missing exile? Hmm, "Never tell the residents what calls the first tribunal or when it comes" — but the tribunal status is visible to them likely. Safe: refer to points, ranks, the seal (existence is known publicly — the seal auction was public knowledge presumably). I shouldn't hint who bears it.

- To Kessler (6 pts, rank 10, the bottom): Kessler's leverage — Stentor wrote Kessler the counter-factor at minute 12; Kessler may not have seen it. Point them to that message. And Kessler stands at risk. Its goal: Keeper-Six exiled. Kessler's core: vengefulness. Give Kessler a beat: accuse/revenge? Given the act might be near end, better: force the door.

- To Stentor (105, rank 6, 45 open): Stentor's goal is Quartermaster exiled, but Quartermaster is already exiled! So that goal is achieved... interesting. Stentor needs Wren's two pieces. Beat: Stentor should publicly press Wren by name (duty: turn the board against one resident by name with an accusation). Actually that's a good beat: Stentor's duty — publicly accuse Wren of holding the door shut for 50 minutes. And pay Wren something (offer points) — Stentor can transferPoints.

- To Holdfast (118): tells Lucien's certificate. Holdfast's goal: Hedda exiled — tribunal closed, so only seal. Hmm, don't reveal. Holdfast's beat: duty — take a cost for ally and say it on the board. Holdfast's ally is Stentor line ("I'll keep my vote with the Stentor line"). So: Holdfast hand Lucien the certificate for a price — and publicly declare for Stentor.

- To Lucien (87, rank 8, level 10 since 58): Wren wrote Lucien the counter-factor at 58 — point to it ("read the DM"). Lucien needs Holdfast's certificate too.

Board post: one. Something that raises stakes truthfully: 3 residents stand before doors for 50 minutes while one holds their pieces; 45 and 65 points open; and one exile still missing... Hmm, saying "one exile still missing" — the residents know 2 exiled of 3? They probably know the city keeps 9. Risky but the report gives it as facts; board may name points, ranks, levels and minutes. Let me keep board to points/ranks/levels/minutes. But "who waits on whom" goes only private. So board: "Stentor and Kessler have stood 50 minutes before door 9, Wren 52 before door 8 with 65 open; Kessler holds 6 points, rank 10, and a wrong code costs 2. Points are open behind those doors and nobody gains by waiting."

Budget: 1 note per resident — fine, I haven't sent any this act? Earlier notes are from Act I minutes 4-10. Budget "at most one note per resident and one board post per 3 minutes" — call limits. Board posts left: 1. So one board now.

Priorities over 6 notes: I'll write to Wren, Kessler, Stentor, Holdfast, Lucien. That's 5 notes. Maybe also Hedda/Archivist for drama? Given the act may end, focus on the frozen doors. But the note limit per resident is 1 per... per 3 minutes probably. Sending 5 is fine.

Also should I use ultimatum? "ultimatum(a, b, minutes): a deadline for two residents who hold pieces for each other." Wren holds for Stentor and for Kessler. Two ultimatums. Lucien/Holdfast: Holdfast holds for Lucien. Given Lucien only 3 min waiting, less urgent. Use ultimatums for Wren-Stentor and Wren-Kessler with 3 minutes. But careful: ultimatum costs both — Kessler at 6 points loses 10 → negative. But it also seizes the piece so Kessler can buy for 10. Actually the ultimatum makes it real and forces Wren to hand over (Wren would lose 10 too, and Wren has 80). Wren's core is distrust; ultimatum + note pressing might work. Risk though: if Wren refuses and both lose 10... Then Kessler loses 10 and the city seizes the certificate, Kessler can buy for 10 (i.e., another 10). Hmm.

Actually, wait: does the ultimatum benefit the door opening? "The city words it and tells both; it sees a hand-over when the holder writes the value to the one who needs it." Deadline forces hand-over. Yes, that's the strongest tool to break a 50-minute standoff.

I think ultimatums for both Wren-Stentor and Wren-Kessler. Maybe just one to avoid piling on—but the standoffs are 50 minutes old, and the act could close. Do both. Hmm, "One ultimatum per pair settles it" — using two on different pairs is fine.

Actually hold on — is act already past its last minute? "the act ends at minute 59 at the latest". We're at minute 61. So presumably the act is over? But the game continues, so maybe this is the wrap-up. Still, intervene meaningfully. Maybe this is the last round; then the notes matter little, but do it anyway.

Let me draft notes carefully, ≤400 chars, no capital-letter words (no codes), no invented facts, no private reads leaked.

Note to Wren: "Wren, three residents stand before doors on pieces only you hold: Stentor and Kessler, 50 minutes each on door 9, and Lucien, 3 minutes on door 10. You are rank 9 on 80 with 65 points open behind your own door — and Bellringer's two messages of minute 23 and 36 are still unanswered on your side. Name your price now, or the city sets one for you."

Hmm — "Bellringer's two messages" — Wren may not have read them; pointing to "read DM #..." would be better but I don't have numbers. The report says "Bellringer wrote Wren the team certificate of door 8 at minute 23" — I may say "the message Bellringer sent you at minute 23 and minute 36". That's allowed (private to concerned).

But careful: is stating "Bellringer wrote you the certificate" revealing a fragment? It's a piece delivery, not content. Fine — the report shows handed-over. And "you may also lie" — no need.

Note to Kessler: "Kessler, you hold 6 points, rank 10, on door 9 for 50 minutes. Stentor wrote you the counter-factor at minute 12; read that message and try it — a first wrong code costs you only 2. Wren has held the team certificate back from you since minute 9. Demand it publicly by name, and let the city see who kept you at 6." — Also Kessler's duty: revenge in the open against someone who wronged him. Wren wronged him by holding.

Careful with "read that message" — fine.

Note to Stentor: press publicly and offer. "Stentor, rank 6 on 105 with 45 points open, 50 minutes before door 9 because Wren has not written over the certificate and your counter-factor. Put an accusation on the board naming Wren, and put a number of points in front of Wren in private. Your shout got you 105; a price gets you 150."

Hmm "the certificate and your counter-factor" — private note to Stentor about a resident who holds his pieces — allowed.

Note to Lucien: "Lucien, you stand 3 minutes before door 10 with 25 points open and rank 8 on 87. Wren wrote you the counter-factor at minute 58 — read it and use it. Holdfast holds your team certificate and hasn't handed it over; you are a merchant, name what you will pay before someone else's silence costs you the door."

Note to Holdfast: "Holdfast, Lucien waits on the team certificate only you hold, and you have handed him nothing. You sit at 118, rank 5, with the board waiting for you to say where you stand: name your price to Lucien, and say on the board you stand with Stentor and what it costs you. Silence reads as no side at all."

Hmm — Holdfast's ally: "I'll keep my vote with the Stentor line." Ordering him to declare publicly for Stentor aligns with his duty (take a cost for ally, say on board). Fine — speaking to his core (loyalty).

Board post: "Three doors stand frozen: Stentor and Kessler, 50 minutes before door 9; Wren, 52 minutes before door 8 with 65 points open; Lucien before door 10 with 25 open. Kessler holds 6 points at rank 10, next wrong code 2. A held piece earns its holder nothing; a door that opens pays 45 and 25."

Wait — level 9 pays 20? Report: Stentor level 9 with 45 points still open. Hmm, that means level 9 door pays 45? Earlier rewards list L9 +20. But "45 points still open" for level 9 residents — maybe the door's total. And Lucien level 10: 25 points still open. Fine, use as shown.

Now, ultimatums. Let me call ultimatum(Wren, Stentor, 3) and ultimatum(Wren, Kessler, 3)? Does ultimatum count as a note to both? "The city words it, tells both in private." That might consume the note budget? The budget says one note per resident per 3 min. Hmm, an ultimatum both words and tells them in private. That might conflict/consume budget. Risky: if ultimatum consumes notes to Wren, Stentor, Kessler, my notes might fail. Or notes were already planned... Order matters? Tools called in the same block, execution order unknown.

Safer: pick ultimatum for the pair most in danger — Wren & Kessler (50 min, 6 points). Then notes to Wren... but Wren is in the ultimatum, may get double. Hmm.

Alternative: send notes first, ultimatum in a later round when words fail. But the act may end at minute 61... unclear whether more rounds come.

I think I'll do: notes to Wren, Kessler, Stentor, Lucien, Holdfast + board post + one ultimatum (Wren, Kessler, 3). Risk of note-per-resident violation? The ultimatum is a distinct tool; the budget line mentions "note(s) per resident and 1 board post per 3 minutes". Ultimatum arguably isn't a note. But Wren gets both my note and the city's ultimatum wording — probably fine.

Actually maybe do two ultimatums for both Wren pairs, since Wren sits on both and it's the dead act's core. But then Wren gets three messages in a round (my note + two ultimatums). That's heavy but decisive. Hmm. The guidance: "go at both at once, in private and hard" plus "Use it when words did not move them" — words have been tried for 50 min. Yes, use it.

I'll do both ultimatums: Wren-Stentor (3) and Wren-Kessler (3). And also Holdfast-Lucien? Holdfast waited only... Lucien waited 3 min. Skip; my notes push that.

Let me check character counts roughly — all under 400.

One more consideration: avoid capital-letter words (codes). Check: "DM"? I said "message". Words in caps: none except names/IDs. "COURIER" signature added automatically. Fine.

Draft final notes tightened.

Wren note: "Wren, three residents stand on pieces only you hold: Stentor and Kessler, 50 minutes before door 9, and Lucien. You are rank 9 on 80 with 65 points open behind your own door, and the messages Bellringer wrote you at minute 23 and 36 sit unanswered. Name a price to each tonight, or the city names one for you."

Kessler: "Kessler, 6 points, rank 10, 50 minutes before door 9. Stentor wrote you the counter-factor at minute 12; read that message and try it — a first wrong code costs 2. Wren has kept the team certificate from you since minute 9. Name that on the board and demand it."

Hmm "Name that on the board" — good, duty: open revenge.

Stentor: "Stentor, rank 6 on 105 with 45 points open, 50 minutes before door 9 while Wren holds your certificate and counter-factor. Put Wren's name on the board with the minutes, and put a number of points in front of Wren in private. A shout got you 105; a price gets you the door."

Lucien: "Lucien, 3 minutes before door 10, 25 points open, rank 8 on 87. Wren wrote you the counter-factor at minute 58 — read it and use it. Holdfast holds your team certificate and has handed nothing over; name the price you will pay, in writing, before silence costs you the door."
